package_info.why_malicious: These versions were published after an npm account takeover and contain injected code that surreptitiously reroutes users’ cryptocurrency transactions to an attacker-controlled wallet, resulting in direct financial theft.

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (exact filename not specified, but within the Ledger Connect Kit npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the transaction process, intercepts outgoing crypto transactions, modifies the destination address to an attacker-controlled wallet, and sends the altered transaction, resulting in user funds being stolen.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and modifying transaction destinations is a classic sign of a wallet drainer or crypto-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal wallet connection libraries should only facilitate user-approved transactions, not alter transaction data or redirect funds.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate transaction signing libraries may inspect or validate transactions, but never silently change the recipient address.
key_indicators: Injection of a rogue WalletConnect dependency
Silent redirection of funds to attacker wallet

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to npm account of former Ledger employee and publishes new package versions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed via npm

attack_chain.action: Malicious versions (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) are installed by dApps and users.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in user environments

attack_chain.action: Injected code hooks into wallet transaction process and reroutes funds to attacker wallet.

behavioral_signatures: Runtime interception and modification of crypto transaction data
Injection or use of rogue dependencies (e.g., WalletConnect variants)
Redirection of transaction destination addresses to hardcoded or attacker-controlled values
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or modified WalletConnect dependencies
Discrepancy between npm package versions and Git tags/releases
Unexpected changes in main package JavaScript files in specific versions
network_indicators: Transactions sent to previously unseen or suspicious wallet addresses
Outbound network requests to attacker-controlled infrastructure (if exfiltration or C2 is present)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mismatches between npm package versions and corresponding Git tags/releases, especially for high-value or widely used packages. Analyze package contents for injected or modified dependencies (e.g., rogue WalletConnect). At runtime, detect code that intercepts and alters transaction data, particularly changes to destination wallet addresses. Flag any package versions that introduce such behavior or dependencies not present in the official repository.
